articles.headline: Jaguars collect Travis Hunter's first INT ball after spat
articles.description: Jaguars cornerback Travis Hunter ended up with the football from his first NFL interception.
articles.body:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Jaguars cornerback Travis Hunter ended up with the football from his first NFL interception.

Hunter spun the ball in celebration and then danced in the end zone after picking off a pass from New England's Drake Maye late in the second quarter Sunday. A Patriots ball boy picked it up and refused to give it to Jaguars veteran defensive end Josh Hines-Allen, even screaming, "Hey, you can't touch me" when Hines-Allen tried to grab the ball. The ball boy appeared to try to push Hines-Allen away.

NFL players are allowed to keep game balls, although they get charged a hefty price by the league.

Hines-Allen tried to knock this one out of the ball boy's hands before Jacksonville's equipment manager, George Pellicer, stepped between them. The ball boy again screamed, "Hey, he pushed me. He can't do that" as Pellicer worked to retrieve the ball.

The Jaguars confirmed Monday that they did end up getting the football.

Video of the interaction went viral after the game, which the Jaguars won 35-6.

"I was just talking about it," Jaguars coach Liam Coen said during a Zoom call with reporters Monday. "I haven't gotten a clean answer. We've been in communication with those guys over there. I think they've gotten it sorted out; I can't say for certain if we got the actual ball or not.

"I know there was something that went on there. I think it's all squared away. We'll get it taken care of."

Hunter, the 2025 Heisman Trophy winner and No. 2 pick from Colorado, made a leaping catch on the pass intended for Patriots receiver Efton Chism III. The play prevented New England from cutting into a 14-3 lead just before the break.

"The coach did a great job scheming it up for us," Hunter said after the game. "He called the perfect call for us. We all talked and we communicated on my side of the ball, and I just made it happen."

articles.headline: Warriors' Steph Curry on choosing to extend: 'This is home'
articles.description: Stephen Curry called Golden State "home" in his first public appearance since signing a two-year, $116 million extension with the Warriors.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO -- In his first public appearance since signing a two-year, $116 million extension with the Golden State Warriors, superstar point guard Stephen Curry explained why he decided to recommit to the only NBA franchise he's ever known.

"This is home," Curry said. "This is what we've built. This is a community that I've played in front of my entire career. Being able to finish the story the right way is a big part of what I can control."

Curry entered the offseason on a one-year, $62.6 million expiring contract. He became eligible for an extension on Aug. 29 and general manager Mike Dunleavy immediately gave Curry a menu of options, including a contract up to his max or a wait-and-see approach, which would've delivered the front office extra time and financial flexibility.

Curry contemplated for nearly a month and landed on the two-year, $116 million middle ground approach this past Friday, giving him late-career security and the Warriors' some extra financial breathing room.

It's more than $20 million below the two-year, $136.7 million Curry was eligible to sign, but it includes a player option in the second season, so Curry has only truly committed to a $10 million pay-cut for a single season.

"We're all smart people in this room," Curry said. "So you can kind of read the tea leaves on why it's designed the way that it is."

Dunleavy and the Warriors' front office have intentionally loaded their books with large expiring contracts, setting themselves up for an ocean of cap space to either be leveraged near the trade deadline or utilized next summer.

Curry's $55.7 million contract for 2027-28 cuts that theoretical cap space nearly in half, but the $10 million pay-cut is enough of a gift to give the Warriors some extra cushion in their planning.

"I'm not fast-forwarding to February," Curry said. "I'm not fast-forwarding to next offseason. None of that. It's start game one, try to win. If we're competitive and doing what we're supposed to do, then that's information learned on how we need to get better."

The already wounded Warriors were delivered an extra bit of bad news on Monday. Starting center Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely with another "health issue," as Dunleavy termed it, after missing large chunks of the past two seasons with a mysterious illness.

Porzingis will not travel with the team to Hawai'i on Monday night, ruling him out for the first four practices of training camp and the preseason opener next Sunday against the LA Clippers in Honolulu.

"I'm not marking him down as being out to start the (regular) season or anything like that," Dunleavy said. "He's just not available this week."

The Warriors are already without starting wings Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody, both limited to individual light court work in the middle stages of rehab for significant knee injuries. They won't be back in the lineup for multiple months.

articles.body:
The 2026-27 NBA season officially kicked off Tuesday as the Houston Rockets held their media day, before the Dallas Mavericks followed suit Friday.

The other 28 teams in the association joined them Monday, ahead of training camps beginning for most teams.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first media day away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their first impressions?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Quick links:

Free agency grades | Trade grades

Trade tracker | Transactions | Offseason buzz

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Sept. 28

Doncic talks LeBron exit, Lakers "championship" ceiling

Speaking to ESPN's Brian Windhorst during Los Angeles Lakers media day, guard Luka Doncic detailed his reaction to LeBron James leaving for the Philadelphia 76ers this past summer and why he thinks a successful 2026-27 includes a Lakers run to the title.

"It was kind of sad. Playing with LeBron was amazing. There's a lot of things I learned from him. ... We all know who LeBron James is."

Shams: Duren's relationship with Pistons "has fractures"

Simmons 'didn't touch a ball for a year'

During Sacramento Kings media day, guard Ben Simmons laid out the reasons he chose the Kings and why he's excited for the 2026-27 season.

"The expectations are low. I feel like that's been something on me too, so we can relate in that way," Simmons told reporters. "I think we have a chip on our shoulder."

Simmons last played in 2024-25, appearing in 51 games for the Brooklyn Nets and LA Clippers. The three-time All-Star said the time away gave him the chance to focus on "getting my body right and my mind right."

Pistons GM hasn't spoken with Duren all summer ahead of big decision

Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons have a decision to make as the clock ticks closer to Oct. 1 -- the deadline to sign a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer.

For Duren, he can accept the five-year, $200 million contract that has been offered by Detroit or he can become the first player named All-NBA or All-Star to sign the qualifying offer. If he chooses the latter, Duren would hold veto power on any trade this season and is an unrestricted free agent next summer.

For the Pistons, weighing the risk of having an All-NBA player on a one-year contract and, more importantly, the likelihood he will depart next summer as a free agent, is key.

There are eight projected teams who have significant cap space to sign Duren to a four-year, $189 million max contract.

"I can't control the different things that he does or his group does," president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said at Media Day. "For me, it's control what we can and letting him know he is a big part of what we do."

Langdon also said he hasn't spoken with Duren all summer during the Pistons' Media Day.

articles.headline: Jokic leaves no doubt on future: 'I'm going to sign next year'
articles.description: Nikola Jokic left little doubt that he plans to be back in Denver at least next season after saying he plans to sign his extension when it's offered next summer.
articles.body:
Nikola Jokic left no doubt on media day about his future with the Denver Nuggets as he enters the final guaranteed year of his contract.

"I'm going to sign next year," Jokic said Monday.

"If they want me," he added.

There's little doubt from Denver's side that it will. The three-time MVP has a player option for next season and was eligible to negotiate a four-year, $278 million extension this offseason. By waiting to sign, Jokic will be able to ink a five-year, $359.5 million contract next summer.

Jokic said he has talked with the leadership team in Denver, including executive vice president of basketball operations Ben Tenzer, executive vice president of player personnel John Wallace and governor Josh Kroenke.

"They know my opinion, and I was being more than open about it, and hopefully they trust me," Jokic said.

The Nuggets are coming off a disappointing postseason finish, losing to the Minnesota Timberwolves in the first round. Denver has yet to make it past the second round since winning the franchise's first championship in 2023.

The end of the roster has been reshuffled, with restricted free agent Peyton Watson getting moved in a deal to Cleveland. To supplement the bench, the Nuggets re-signed Spencer Jones and added guard Tyus Jones and center Marvin Bagley III.

articles.headline: Lillard: Blazers' crowded backcourt 'will work itself out'
articles.description: Damian Lillard said he's not worried about balancing a backcourt that includes himself, Ja Morant, Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson, saying it "will work itself out."
articles.body:
PORTLAND -- Damian Lillard asked to be traded from the Portland Trail Blazers in the summer of 2023 because he didn't feel the team had a realistic chance to contend and needed to rebuild. The team did just that while he was away for two seasons with the Milwaukee Bucks and out all of last season recovering from a ruptured Achilles' tendon.

Now that he's back on the court for the Blazers, the question is how new coach Micah Nori will make the surplus of backcourt talent fit together.

"If we are just doing the right thing, playing the right way ... I think the balance will work itself out," Lillard said, when asked how the team will deploy newly-acquired, former All Star guard Ja Morant, former lottery pick Scoot Henderson and two-time NBA champion Jrue Holiday.

"If our mentality is right and we handle it right, I think we could be a tough time for everybody," Lillard added. "If I get the ball and I'm advancing the ball ahead to Ja Morant, I feel pretty good about it. If I'm advancing the ball to [All Star forward] Deni [Avdija] out there, I feel good about it. And for both of those guys, if they are attacking the rim, attacking the paint and they're kicking the ball out to me for a 3-pointer, I think they should feel great about that."

Lillard, 35, missed all of last season recovering from a torn Achilles that he suffered in his final game with the Milwaukee Bucks. The only public glimpse of him in a Blazers uniform came at the All-Star game in Los Angeles when he won the 3-point contest. He's been spotted in workout videos looking very much like his old self on the court. Monday he said that he's been fully recovered from his injury for several months and only thinks about it when he's asked.

"I don't have any restrictions," he said. "I talk about the injury when I'm asked about it, but when I'm playing, it's not a thought anymore. I'm at that stage. I'm able to play free."

 

Nori, who was hired after a protracted and controversial coaching search led by a mandate by new owner Tom Dundon to control costs, said that he and Lillard have spent a lot of early mornings in the Trail Blazers facility talking about the team and the potential it has.

"Dame literally just wants to win, I think that's the only thing left he really has to do," Nori said. "As far as physically, I've seen him in the gym and the individual workouts. ...He's in as good a shape as he's been in, like he's told me, in his whole career."

As far as balancing the guard-heavy roster, Nori and general manager Joe Cronin suggested that Holiday could see some time on the wing -- noting he defended San Antonio center Victor Wembanyama during last season's first-round playoff series. Nori also noted that an abundance of ballhandlers -- which also includes Avdija, who was put into more of a point forward role by former head coach Tiago Splitter last year -- will help take some of the load off of Lillard.

articles.headline: J.J. McCarthy traded to Giants: Will he succeed in New York?
articles.description: With Jaxson Dart out for the season, the Giants dealt a fifth-round pick to Minnesota for McCarthy. But does this move the needle for New York? Can it work?
articles.body:
After Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending knee injury in Week 2, it was probably inevitable that the Giants would add another quarterback to their roster. Jameis Winston can be combustible at his best, and while the weather wasn't great at MetLife Stadium yesterday, he has averaged 4.7 yards per attempt and completed 51% of his passes since inheriting the starting job. With Jake Haener as the only other QB on the roster, getting someone to backup Winston and potentially take over if he continues to struggle was a no-brainer for the Giants.

And while Giants fans might have loved the idea of adding someone like Joe Flacco to continue the veteran's tour of Northeast football, teams weren't about to trade a useful backup who was one injury away from being their starter to the Giants out of pity. The market was QB3s, not QB2s, which left one very clear choice for New York: J.J. McCarthy

Landing a fifth-round pick for McCarthy was an obvious call for the Vikings. Once their quarterback of the future after they traded up to take him in the first round of the 2024 draft, McCarthy had quickly and brutally fallen out of favor in Minnesota. After being the NFC Offensive Player of the Week in his NFL debut last season -- an opening-week win over the Bears -- McCarthy's inability to work all areas of the field, operate within the structure of the offense or avoid negative plays frustrated a Vikings organization that had let Sam Darnold leave in free agency to hand the job to him.

Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show'

While it was no surprise when McCarthy lost something resembling a QB competition to new starter Kyler Murray in training camp this summer, the writing was really on the wall once it became clear that Kevin O'Connell preferred Carson Wentz as his second option. Trading McCarthy netted some small amount of draft capital for the Vikings while also saving them $4.6 million over the next two years in the process.

So, the trade makes sense for both organizations. Will it work out for McCarthy, who is still only 23 years old and younger than Ty Simpson, whom the Rams took with their first-round pick in this year's draft? We're living in a bit of a golden era of second (or third) acts for quarterbacks around the NFL, with the likes of Darnold, Bryce Young, Malik Willis, Baker Mayfield and others enjoying varying levels of success after their first organization gave up (and/or benched) them before the end of their rookie deals. Could McCarthy be the next to follow in their footsteps and turn his career around after a rough start?

In the wake of the Giants' trade, I'll argue both sides of that question. I'm not sure where I land, but I can see a case for McCarthy thriving in New York, and I can see one where he disappoints Giants fans who are hoping for an answer. articles.headline: Sources: Vikings' Jefferson has ankle sprain, could play this week
articles.description: Vikings star wide receiver Justin Jefferson has an ankle sprain, according to the MRI performed Monday, and there's a chance he'll be able to play Sunday against the Dolphins, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Dan Graziano.
articles.body:
Minnesota Vikings star wide receiver Justin Jefferson has an ankle sprain, according to the MRI performed Monday, and there's a chance he'll be able to play Sunday against the Miami Dolphins, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Dan Graziano.

Jefferson did not return Sunday after suffering a left ankle injury at the end of the Vikings' first possession in a 23-16 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers that improved Minnesota to 3-0 this season.

Coach Kevin O'Connell said after Sunday's game that Jefferson was "pretty close" to returning to the game but "just couldn't get there."

His injury Sunday came at the end of a 10-yard screen pass with 11:07 remaining in the first quarter. He had earlier caught a 22-yard pass across the middle amid high hopes that he and Kyler Murray would team up to elevate the passing game.

In his absence, receiver Jordan Addison caught five passes for 90 yards, including a 41-yard touchdown from Murray in the second quarter. But it was the only offensive touchdown the Vikings scored Sunday as they managed just seven first downs after Jefferson's injury.

At one point after the injury, Murray completed only two of 15 passes. He finished the day with 15 completions in 29 attempts for 168 yards, taking three sacks and having a batted pass intercepted in the backfield.

Jefferson, a two-time first-team All-Pro and four-time Pro Bowl selection, has largely been healthy in his NFL career and has played in every Vikings game for five of his six full seasons. The lone exception was a torn right hamstring in 2023 that caused him to miss seven games.

ESPN's Kevin Seifert contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Sources: Jets RB Breece Hall week-to-week with quad injury
articles.description: Jets running back Breece Hall, who suffered a quad injury in Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Lions, is considered week-to-week, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- New York Jets running back Breece Hall, who injured his right quadriceps Sunday, is considered week-to-week, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and the NFL Network's Ian Rapoport on Monday.

There was some sense of relief, as an MRI showed that Hall avoided a long-term injury, a source said. Nevertheless, he likely won't be ready to play Sunday against the Chicago Bears, a blow to the Jets' already struggling rushing attack.

After a 152-yard rushing day in the opener, the Jets (1-2) managed only 67 and 58 yards in Weeks 2 and 3, including only 61 yards on 29 carries (2.1-yard average) for Hall. The Jets will lean heavily on third-year backs Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis while Hall is sidelined.

Injuries are mounting for the Jets, who played without wide receiver Adonai Mitchell (finger) and tight end Mason Taylor (thumb) in Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Detroit Lions. Their status for Sunday is uncertain.

Coach Aaron Glenn provided no update Monday on Hall or left guard Dylan Parham (knee), who also was injured Sunday.

"[The run game] is one area that we have to fix," said Glenn, adding there's an "urgency in trying to make sure that we get that done, because that's been a strong point of ours, especially after the first game. To have these two games to where we didn't run it as well, that's something that we have to dial into to make sure that we get those things fixed."

The Jets identified Hall as a foundational piece on offense, signing him to a three-year, $43.5 million extension in the offseason. He missed three weeks in training camp due to a strained groin but came out hot in the opener with a 102-yard, one-touchdown game in the 23-10 win over the Tennessee Titans.

On his 13th and final carry in Detroit, Hall was tackled out of bounds early in the fourth quarter and rolled over in pain, clutching his right thigh.

After the game, Hall said he "felt something when I was running and then got tackled and planted and then felt something else."
